punchline: Two statisticians mailed a questionnaire and counted who got sick.
thirty_sec: In 1950 Richard Doll and Austin Bradford Hill compared smoking habits of 709 patients in 20 London hospitals. In October 1951 they mailed questionnaires to British doctors and followed 34,439 men for decades; the 1956 follow-up is cited as statistical proof that smoking causes lung cancer.
question: What suspicion about your work could you start counting this week?
key_contrast: A vivid anecdote versus a patient count.
